# My Knee Score

> A free knee health questionnaire at mykneescore.com. Ten questions, about five
> minutes, and a score out of 100 with guidance on what to do next. Static HTML,
> no backend, no accounts, nothing stored. Part of the OmKnee group alongside
> mykneescan.com, sportshealing.com and omkneehealth.com.

Last updated 4 October 2026. Scoring: Short Knee Score v2.0.

## How the score works

Ten questions, each answered on a 0 to 10 scale where 10 is best, presented as
five options worth 10, 7.5, 5, 2.5 and 0. Each question carries a fixed weight.
The weights sum to 1.00. The weighted total multiplied by ten, rounded, gives a
score from 0 to 100. Scoring runs in the browser; nothing is sent anywhere.

Bands: Optimal 85 to 100, Good 70 to 84, Fair 60 to 69, Pay attention 0 to 59.

The questionnaire has not been clinically validated. It is educational, not a
diagnosis. Red flag symptoms, meaning sudden injury, locking, giving way or a
hot swollen knee, warrant prompt medical review whatever the score says.

## Pages

- [Home and questionnaire](https://mykneescore.com/index.html): the landing page, the score bands, progress tracking, and the full ten question test in an overlay.
- [Knee anatomy](https://mykneescore.com/anatomy.html): bones, ligaments and cartilage as plain language cards, with a labelled diagram and red flag guidance.
- [Advanced scores](https://mykneescore.com/advanced/index.html): a hub of published knee outcome measures, each on its own page with a working calculator, interpretation, citation and licence. Reached from the top menu and a footer link; nothing on the home page promotes it.

## The Advanced section

Separate from the Short Knee Score and built from a different source. Ports
the calculators from the kneescore-research project, with the arithmetic
unchanged and checked by a parity test against the originals. Most scores use
a generic engine; SK11 and PK7 use their own weighted engines. The Oxford Knee
Score and WOMAC are held back pending licence permission.

Unlike the two pages above, the Advanced pages share one stylesheet at
advanced/assets/advanced.css and are generated by a build script in
tools/advanced/.

## Conventions

- Static files served from GitHub Pages.
- The home and anatomy pages are self contained: CSS in a style block, JS in a
  script block, no build step. Every colour is a token in their `:root` block,
  with no colour literals elsewhere.
- The Advanced pages do not follow those two rules. They share a stylesheet and
  are generated, and that stylesheet holds a fourth copy of the design tokens
  under different names.
- UK spelling. No em dashes anywhere in the source.

## Not here yet

- Score history. Nothing is saved between visits; users are told to note their score.
- A Terms and Conditions page.
- A How It Works page setting out the evidence base.
- A markdown twin of each page. These are hand written files with no build step, so a twin would drift.
